sections.html:
McCandless is a home rule municipality in Allegheny County, officially the Town of McCandless, in Pittsburgh's North Hills. A sale there carries a 2.5 percent combined transfer tax. The town also issues its own lien letter and points sellers to the sanitary authority for a dye test.

About 29,709 people live here, and the population has been flat for decades, so your listing competes with a mature, established housing supply. Hilly ground defines most streets, and Pine Creek runs through a valley in the middle of town with a floodplain along it. Homes near the creek deserve a floodplain check, so ask the town whether your lot sits in the mapped floodplain before you write the listing description.

Public schools belong to the North Allegheny School District. Buyers often search by named plan or community, such as Meadow Oaks, Guyton Farms, Greybrooke, Bennington Woods, Pin Oak, Briarwood, Park Meadows, Foxcroft Village, Sample Manor, Colington Square, Royal Manor, Pinnacle Pointe, Longvue Acres or Allison Park. Several ZIP codes cover the town, so confirm the municipality on the tax bill, not the postal city, before checking local rules.

sections.h2: What the transfer tax is when you sell in McCandless
sections.html:
The total realty transfer tax on a McCandless sale is 2.5 percent. That combines the state's 1 percent, a 1 percent municipal share and a one half of 1 percent North Allegheny School District share, based on the county's published rate table.

The county collects the tax when the deed is recorded. Buyer and seller are both liable, and contracts decide the split. Build the rate into your net sheet before you compare offers. Some transfers, including certain deeds between family members and property passed through an estate, are exempt from the state portion, so ask the county's Real Estate office how an exemption is documented.

sections.h2: Lien letter, dye test and utility liens
sections.html:
A seller should order a municipal lien letter and arrange a dye test. The lien letter costs $30 by mail or $35 if the results are emailed, and the request needs the owner's name, property address, parcel number and the reason, such as a sale. Checks are payable to the Town of McCandless.

The sanitary authority and the water authority can each file liens for unpaid service, so call both before the closing. The town's tax office handles the lien letter request at 412-364-0616.

sections.h2: How real estate taxes are billed in McCandless
sections.html:
The deputy tax collector, Jordan Tax Service, collects both Town and North Allegheny School District real estate tax. Beginning in 2026, owners receive two separate invoices, one for the Town and one for the school district.

  • The Town millage for 2026 is 1.236 mills.
  • The North Allegheny School District rate is 20.43 mills for the 2025 to 2026 school year, or $2,043 per $100,000 of assessed value.
  • Allegheny County lists 6.43 mills.
  • Taxes unpaid after December 31 are delinquent and can lead to a lien on the property.

An installment plan with three equal payments is open only to owners with a homestead or farmstead exclusion. The first payment is due August 31, followed by October 31 and December 31, and late installments carry a 10 percent penalty. Owners approved for the Act 77 senior citizen discount receive 30 percent off the Town portion. Pay tax on time even while an appeal is pending, because the higher amount must be paid once a deadline passes.

Payments cannot be left in the Town Hall drop box. Send them to Jordan Tax Service or use the options printed on the statement. Jordan representatives also sit at Town Hall on select dates, which are posted on the Town calendar, and owners should bring the full tax statements. Earned income tax and business privilege tax are handled separately by the Keystone Collections Group.

The annual appeal window runs from July 1 through September 1. The Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review hears appeals, and it sends residential hearing notices at least 14 days ahead.

If you miss the window, ask the Office of Property Assessments about the next annual period and about special appeals tied to a change notice. A documented appeal can support a price discussion with a buyer, so gather comparable sales before you file.

Begin by requesting the municipal lien letter, since the town's tax office needs your name, address, parcel number and the reason for the request. Book the dye test with the sanitary authority at the same time, because a failed test can mean sewer lateral work that has to be sorted out before settlement. Then call the sanitary authority and the water authority and ask whether any unpaid service could become a lien.

Look at your tax position as well. Taxes unpaid after December 31 are delinquent, and the Town and school district now send separate invoices, so make sure both are current. When an offer comes in, the title company prorates the Town and school taxes and the county records the deed. If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, tell them about the sale.

sections.h2: Listing or cash purchase in McCandless
sections.html:
Cash works best when the house needs repairs or the closing date matters more than the last dollar of price. A listing suits a house in good condition in a popular plan, where several buyers may compete.

  • Get the lien letter and dye test started before you accept any offer.
  • Compare offers after the 2.5 percent transfer tax, any payoff and the unpaid portion of the year's Town and school taxes.
  • Ask each buyer how they treat the dye test result if the sewer lateral needs work.

A cash sale skips showings, a buyer's loan approval and most repair negotiation. The town's lien letter, the dye test and the transfer tax still apply, so ask the buyer to confirm in writing who orders each one. If the dye test shows a problem with the sewer lateral, you can fix it before closing, price the repair into the offer, or ask the buyer to take the house as it is.

Hilly lots and older drainage are common here, so a buyer's inspector will look at the basement and the ground around the foundation. Have repair records ready, along with your latest tax statements from the Town and the school district, so the buyer sees a clean file from the first conversation.

Cash Home Buyers CA can give you a cash figure to compare with a listing.

faqs.q: What is the total transfer tax in McCandless?
faqs.a: 2.5 percent. The state charges 1 percent, McCandless charges 1 percent, and the North Allegheny School District charges one half of 1 percent.

faqs.q: How do I get a lien letter from the Town of McCandless?
faqs.a: Mail a request with the owner's name, address, parcel number and reason, along with a $30 check. The email option costs $35. Write the check to the Town of McCandless.

faqs.q: Who collects real estate tax in McCandless?
faqs.a: Jordan Tax Service collects both Town and North Allegheny School District real estate tax. Owners receive two separate invoices starting in 2026.
North Allegheny School District. McCandless is also part of the shared Northland Public Library.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Allegheny County assessment?
faqs.a: The annual appeal window runs from July 1 to September 1. If you miss it, contact the county's Office of Property Assessments about later options.
